description: Shared-rule candidates found while authoring skills.logic.json — inlined there for now; the integrator may merge these into data/logic_rules.json (same shape as a logic_rules entry).

candidates.name: Skill rides on the action family
candidates.description: A skill with action_type `family` may be played when the caster's action is that code, or — for Move and Posture skills — an empty action (EP / EM), per peer.mjs ridesFor(). Repeated in every one of the 14 skill prerequisites.

candidates.name: Permanent not already in the holding
candidates.description: A permanent skill / effect may only be played while it is not yet among the caster's permanents. Used by the 5 permanent skills; the effects collection has the same need.

candidates.name: Target is an enemy in contact
candidates.description: in_contact AND is_enemy — the single most repeated prerequisite across skills, classes and actions (A-skills, Bluff, Counter Spell, Priest, Witch, Manipulator, Avenger, Attack, Combo).

candidates.name: Target is an ally (or self) in contact
candidates.description: in_contact AND is_ally — Healer, Overlord, Warrior, Transmuter, Trade.

candidates.name: Rule 8 pc override over the `outcome` context
candidates.description: rule_8_instant_returns bound to the round-maths context the resolver supplies: outcome.took_with / took_without / dealt_with / dealt_without (healed_* default 0). Repeated verbatim in the 9 non-permanent skills.

candidates.name: point_buy_stat vocabulary
candidates.description: Values a skill's point_buy_stat may take besides null: 'any' (roll against the highest stat) or a stat key in either spelling the data uses (stat_vitality … / vitality …). Used in all 14 skill validations.

candidates.name: Highest of the four stats
candidates.description: The stat an 'any' point-buy rolls against (Sanctuary placement, Druid defence token): max(vitality, world, matter, will).
candidates.note: json-logic cannot path into a param expression; merge as a custom op `stat_max(stats)` or expand with four `stat_of`-style reads of the caller's unit instead.
